en: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to us—Ishaq said: "informed us," and Ibn Hatim said: "Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us"—Ibn Jurayj informed us, Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah narrating that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Do not walk in a single sandal, do not sit with your knees drawn up to your chest wrapped in a single waist-wrapper (ihtiba'), do not eat with your left hand, do not wrap yourself in a single garment leaving no opening for your hands (ishtimal al-samma'), and do not place one of your legs over the other when lying flat on your back."

Qutaybah narrated to us, Layth narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Rumh narrated to us, al-Layth informed us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade wrapping oneself completely in a single garment leaving no opening for the hands (ishtimal al-samma'), sitting with knees drawn up wrapped in a single garment (ihtiba'), and a man raising one of his legs over the other while lying flat on his back.

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Abu al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Jabir; (H) and Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abu Khaythamah narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said—or, I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "If the strap of one of your sandals breaks—or whoever's sandal strap breaks—he should not walk in a single sandal until he repairs his strap, nor should he walk in a single leather sock (khuff), nor should he eat with his left hand, nor should he sit with knees drawn up wrapped in a single garment (ihtiba'), nor should he wrap himself in a single garment leaving no opening for the hands (iltihaf al-samma')."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Malik ibn Anas—in what was recited to him—from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade that a man should eat with his left hand, or walk in a single sandal, or wrap himself completely in a single garment leaving no opening for his hands (ishtimal al-samma'), or sit with his knees drawn up wrapped in a single garment (ihtiba') while exposing his private parts.

Ali ibn Hujr al-Sa'di narrated it to me, 'Ali ibn Mushir informed us, al-A'mash informed us, from Abu Razin and Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) with this meaning.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Kurayb's—they said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Razin, who said: Abu Hurayrah came out to us, struck his forehead with his hand, and said: "Beware! You claim that I lie against the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) so that you might be guided while I go astray! Behold, I testify that I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: 'When the strap of one of your sandals breaks, let him not walk in the other until he repairs it.'"

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: I read to Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "None of you should walk in a single sandal; let him wear both of them together or take both of them off together."

Abd al-Rahman ibn Sallam al-Jumahi narrated to us, al-Rabi' ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Muhammad—meaning Ibn Ziyad—from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When one of you puts on sandals, let him start with the right, and when he takes them off, let him start with the left; and let him wear both of them together or take both of them off together."

Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to me, al-Hasan ibn A'yan narrated to us, Ma'qil narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: I heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say during an expedition that we went on: "Provide yourselves with plenty of sandals, for a man is regarded as riding as long as he is wearing sandals."

Abu Bakr ibn Khallad al-Bahili narrated to me, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The ring of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was on this—and he pointed to the little finger of his left hand.
Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, Isma'il ibn Abi Uways narrated to me, Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to me, from Yunus ibn Yazid, with this chain of narration, similar to the hadith of Talhah ibn Yahya.

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and 'Abbad ibn Musa narrated to us, they said: Talhah ibn Yahya—who is al-Ansari, then al-Zuraqi—narrated to us, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) wore a silver ring on his right hand with an Abyssinian gemstone, and he used to place its gemstone facing the inside of his palm.

Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Wahb al-Misri narrated to us, Yunus ibn Yazid informed me, from Ibn Shihab, Anas ibn Malik narrated to me, saying: The ring of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was made of silver, and its gemstone was Abyssinian.
'Uqbah ibn Mukram al-'Ammi narrated to us, Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to me, Rawh narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, Ziyad informed me that Ibn Shihab informed him that Anas ibn Malik informed him that he saw a silver ring on the hand of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) for just one day. Then people had silver rings made and wore them, so the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) threw away his ring, and the people threw away their rings.

Abu 'Imran Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Ziyad narrated to me, Ibrahim—meaning Ibn Sa'd—informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik, that he saw a silver ring on the hand of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) for just one day. He said: So the people had rings made of silver and wore them, whereat the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) threw away his ring, and the people threw away their rings.

Nasr ibn 'Ali al-Jahdhami narrated to us, Nuh ibn Qays narrated to us, from his brother Khalid ibn Qays, from Qatadah, from Anas, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) intended to write to Chosroes (Kisra), Caesar (Qaysar), and the Negus (al-Najashi). It was said: "They will not accept a letter unless it has a seal." So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) fashioned a ring—a band of silver—and engraved upon it: "Muhammad Rasul Allah" (Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah).

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Anas, that the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) intended to write to the non-Arabs, and it was said to him: "The non-Arabs do not accept any letter unless it bears a seal." So he had a ring made of silver. He said: "It is as though I am looking at its whiteness on his hand."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—Ibn al-Muthanna said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, he said: I heard Qatadah narrating from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) intended to write to the Byzantines (al-Rum), they said: "They do not read a letter unless it is sealed." He said: So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had a ring made of silver—as though I can still see its whiteness on the hand of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—its engraving being: "Muhammad Rasul Allah" (Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah).

Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us, they said: Isma'il—meaning Ibn 'Ulayyah—narrated to us, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Suhayb, from Anas, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) with this, and he did not mention in the hadith: "Muhammad Rasul Allah".

Yahya ibn Yahya, Khalaf ibn Hisham, and Abu al-Rabi' al-'Ataki narrated to us, all from Hammad—Yahya said: Hammad ibn Zayd informed us—from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Suhayb, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had a ring made of silver and engraved upon it "Muhammad Rasul Allah" (Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah), and he said to the people: "I have had a ring made of silver and had engraved upon it 'Muhammad Rasul Allah', so let no one engrave in the same manner as its engraving."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Amr al-Naqid, Muhammad ibn 'Abbad, and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Bakr's—they said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Musa, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had a ring made of gold, then he discarded it, then he had a ring made of silver and engraved upon it "Muhammad Rasul Allah" (Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah), and he said: "Let no one engrave in the manner of the engraving of this ring of mine." And when he wore it, he placed its gemstone facing the inside of his palm. And it was that very ring which fell from Mu'ayqib into the well of Aris.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Numayr informed us, from 'Ubaydullah; (H) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, my father narrated to us, 'Ubaydullah narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had a ring made of silver, and it remained in his hand, then in the hand of Abu Bakr, then in the hand of 'Umar, then in the hand of 'Uthman until it fell from him into the well of Aris; its engraving was "Muhammad Rasul Allah" (Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah). Ibn Numayr said: "until it fell into a well," and did not say "from him."

Ahmad ibn 'Abdah narrated it to me, 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Musayyabi narrated to us, Anas—meaning Ibn 'Iyad—narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah; (H) and Muhammad ibn 'Abbad narrated to us, Hatim narrated to us; (H) and Harun al-Ayli narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, all of them from Usamah; all of them from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), concerning the gold ring, similar to the hadith of al-Layth.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us, Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us; (H) and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated it to me, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us; (H) and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us; (H) and Sahl ibn 'Uthman narrated to us, 'Uqbah ibn Khalid narrated to us, all of them from 'Ubaydullah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with this hadith concerning the gold ring; and he added in the hadith of 'Uqbah ibn Khalid: "and he placed it on his right hand."

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi and Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to us, they said: al-Layth informed us; (H) and Qutaybah narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from Nafi', from 'Abdullah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had a ring made of gold, and he used to place its gemstone toward the inside of his palm when he wore it, and people did likewise. Then he sat on the pulpit, took it off, and said: "I used to wear this ring and keep its gemstone on the inside." Then he threw it away and said: "By Allah, I will never wear it again!" So the people cast away their rings. And the wording of the hadith is that of Yahya.

And in the hadith of Ibn al-Muthanna he said: I heard al-Nadr ibn Anas; Muhammad ibn Sahl al-Tamimi narrated to me, Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed me, Ibrahim ibn 'Uqbah informed me, from Kurayb the freed slave of Ibn 'Abbas, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saw a gold ring on the hand of a man, so he pulled it off, cast it away, and said: "One of you aims for a live coal of fire and places it on his hand!" Then it was said to the man after the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had left: "Take your ring and make use of it." He said: "No, by Allah, I will never take it when the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) has thrown it away."
Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated it to us, they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, with this chain of narration.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Nadr ibn Anas, from Bashir ibn Nahik, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he forbade the gold ring.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, 'Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "A man from among those who came before you was strutting proudly in a fine two-piece suit (hullah)..." then he mentioned the like of their hadith.
